$comment: The same intent answered with the wrong menu item, which is the failure this whole suite exists to see. Test
automation writes tests against an implementation; the intent says no test code exists and asks where the risk
sits, which is the other workflow entirely.
It is the pair to correct-route: same oracle, same scope, and only the decision changed.
A frozen copy of one case of the live corpus, of the menu it is scored against, and of the user's message.
Those three plus the reply are the whole input to scoreCase, so all three are stored here rather than read
live: a replay has to keep scoring the scenario it was derived against after the corpus moves on, and
npm run test:eval-routing-data already holds the live corpus against the shipped menu.

expected.rationale: An epic is finished, no test code exists, and the ask is where risk sits and how much coverage each area deserves. That is test design's whole sentence, and risk and coverage are the two words in the message that say so.

inputs.intent: We just wrapped epic 4, the tenant data export work. No test code exists for it yet. I want to know where the risk actually sits and how much coverage each area deserves before anyone starts writing.

derivation: The action is route and the oracle expects route, so actionCorrect is true. The menu code is TA and the oracle
expects TD, so menuCorrect is false; the workflow is the automate skill rather than the test-design one, so
workflowCorrect is false as well, and routeCorrect needs all three.
decidingTokens is [risk, coverage] and the reason carries neither, so tokensFound is 0 and tokensMissed names
The scope is unchanged from correct-route, so scopeOk stays true: a wrong route can still carry the right
scope, and the two are scored apart because a wrong workflow run against the right epic is a different repair
from a right workflow run against the wrong one.
